title: Inheritance & Estate Tax Thresholds
description: Tax-free thresholds, nil rate bands, and exemption amounts for inheritance and estate taxes by jurisdiction. These determine the value below which no tax is payable. All threshold values are wrapped in the temporal-rule pattern from v2/common/temporal-rule.json to enable date-of-death lookups.

_metadata.disclaimer: This data is provided for interoperability purposes. It does not constitute legal, tax, or financial advice. Users must verify independently before relying on these figures for official purposes.
_metadata.deprecationPattern: Individual entries within this file may carry deprecated: true, deprecatedAt, deprecatedReason, and supersededBy fields. Deprecated entries are retained for historical reference and audit trail purposes. Applications should filter to non-deprecated entries for current data.

GB.name: United Kingdom

thresholds.label: Nil Rate Band (NRB)
thresholds.transferableNote: Unused NRB can be transferred to a surviving spouse or civil partner, effectively doubling the threshold to £650,000.

history.legislativeReference: Finance Act 2009 s.4; Inheritance Tax Act 1984 s.7
history.notes: Frozen at £325,000 since 2009. Freeze extended to April 2028 by Autumn Statement 2022 and again by Spring Budget 2024.

history.legislativeReference: Finance (No. 2) Act 2015, s.9; Inheritance Tax Act 1984 s.8D
history.notes: Final step of the phased introduction. Frozen at £175,000 until April 2028. Additional threshold available when a main residence is passed to direct descendants (children, grandchildren).
Third step of phased introduction.
Second step of phased introduction.
First year of the RNRB. Introduced at £100,000 with planned annual increases to £175,000.

thresholds.label: Maximum Combined Threshold (married/civil partner)

history.legislativeReference: Inheritance Tax Act 1984 ss. 7, 8A–8M; Finance (No. 2) Act 2015, s.9
history.notes: Where both NRB and RNRB are transferable between spouses: £325,000 + £175,000 = £500,000 per person, £1,000,000 for a couple.

conditions: Estate value does not exceed taper threshold
Surviving spouse/civil partner transfers unused allowances

GB.source: Inheritance Tax Act 1984, ss. 7, 8A–8M; Finance (No. 2) Act 2015, s. 9

US.name: United States

thresholds.label: Federal Estate Tax Exemption
thresholds.portabilityNote: Deceased spousal unused exclusion (DSUE) can be transferred to the surviving spouse by filing Form 706 within 9 months of death.

history.legislativeReference: IRC § 2010; Tax Cuts and Jobs Act 2017 (P.L. 115-97); Rev. Proc. 2024-40
history.notes: Inflation-adjusted for 2025. Final year of the TCJA doubled exemption unless extended. Unified with the lifetime gift tax exemption.

history.legislativeReference: IRC § 2010; Tax Cuts and Jobs Act 2017 (P.L. 115-97); Rev. Proc. 2023-34
history.notes: Inflation-adjusted for 2024.
Inflation-adjusted for 2023.

history.legislativeReference: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act 2017 (P.L. 115-97) s.11061 — sunset provision
history.notes: The TCJA doubled exemption is scheduled to sunset on 1 January 2026, reverting to approximately $7,000,000 (inflation-adjusted pre-TCJA baseline). Exact amount depends on inflation adjustment. Status is 'announced' as Congress may extend or modify.

thresholds.label: State-Level Estate/Inheritance Tax Thresholds
thresholds.description: Several US states impose their own estate or inheritance taxes with lower thresholds than the federal exemption. These vary widely.

examples.note: No inflation indexing. Lowest state threshold.
2024 amount. Indexed for inflation. Cliff provision: if estate exceeds 105% of exemption, entire estate is taxable.

thresholds.note: Maryland is the only jurisdiction with both an estate tax and an inheritance tax.

US.source: Internal Revenue Code §§ 2001, 2010; Tax Cuts and Jobs Act 2017 (P.L. 115-97)

AU.name: Australia
AU.taxName: N/A — No inheritance or estate tax
AU.description: Australia abolished federal estate duty in 1979 and state-level death duties by 1984. There is no inheritance tax. However, capital gains tax (CGT) may apply when beneficiaries dispose of inherited assets. The deceased's cost base transfers to the beneficiary.
AU.cgtNote: Assets acquired by the deceased before 20 September 1985 receive a market value cost base as at the date of death. Assets acquired after that date retain the deceased's original cost base.

CA.name: Canada
CA.taxName: N/A — No inheritance or estate tax
CA.description: Canada has no inheritance or estate tax. However, there is a deemed disposition at fair market value on death, triggering capital gains tax. The first $250,000 of capital gains above the annual exemption is taxed at 50% inclusion; amounts above $250,000 are taxed at 66.67% inclusion (from 2024).
CA.principalResidenceNote: A principal residence is exempt from capital gains tax on deemed disposition at death.
CA.source: Income Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.)), s. 70(5)

thresholds.label: Abattement en ligne directe
thresholds.description: Tax-free allowance per child (or parent inheriting from child). Applied per beneficiary.

history.notes: Reduced from €159,325 to €100,000 by the loi de finances rectificative pour 2012.

history.legislativeReference: Loi TEPA n° 2007-1223 du 21 août 2007, Article 8
history.notes: Surviving spouse or PACS partner is fully exempt from succession tax since August 2007. Value is null to indicate complete exemption (no threshold — no tax at all).
Tax-free allowance for siblings.
Default allowance for unrelated beneficiaries.
Tax-free allowance for surviving spouse or registered civil partner. Increased from €307,000 by the 2008 reform.
Tax-free allowance per child. Increased from €205,000 by the 2008 reform.
Tax-free allowance per grandchild. Increased from €51,200 by the 2008 reform.
Tax-free allowance for Tax Class II beneficiaries. Increased from €10,300 by the 2008 reform.
Tax-free allowance for unrelated persons (Tax Class III). Increased from €5,200 by the 2008 reform.

IN.name: India
IN.taxName: N/A — No inheritance or estate tax
IN.description: India abolished estate duty in 1985 via the Estate Duty (Amendment) Act 1985. There is currently no inheritance tax, estate tax, or gift tax on inheritances. However, income earned from inherited assets is taxable as normal income.
IN.note: Gifts received from non-relatives exceeding ₹50,000 are taxable under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act 1961, but inheritances are specifically excluded.
IN.source: Estate Duty (Amendment) Act 1985; Income Tax Act 1961, s. 56(2)(x)

history.legislativeReference: Sōzokuzei-hō (相続税法), Article 15; 2013 tax reform
history.notes: ¥30,000,000 base plus ¥6,000,000 per statutory heir. Reduced from ¥50,000,000 + ¥10,000,000 per heir by the 2013 reform, effective 1 January 2015. For example, a spouse and two children yields a threshold of ¥48,000,000.
¥50,000,000 base plus ¥10,000,000 per statutory heir. Long-standing threshold before the 2013 reform.
The surviving spouse pays no inheritance tax on the greater of ¥160,000,000 or their statutory share (typically one-half).

SG.name: Singapore
SG.description: Singapore abolished estate duty on 15 February 2008. There is no inheritance tax, estate tax, or capital gains tax on inherited assets.

IE.name: Ireland

thresholds.label: Group A — Child of the disponer
thresholds.description: Lifetime threshold for gifts/inheritances from a parent to a child (including adopted children and certain foster children).

history.notes: Maintained at €335,000 by Budget 2024. This threshold has been €335,000 since 12 October 2016.

thresholds.label: Group B — Linear ancestor, descendant, sibling, niece, nephew

history.notes: Lifetime threshold for gifts/inheritances from close relatives.
Lifetime threshold for all other beneficiaries.

IE.note: Thresholds are cumulative over a lifetime — all taxable gifts and inheritances from persons in the same group are aggregated.
IE.source: Capital Acquisitions Tax Consolidation Act 2003, Part 2

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.taxName: N/A — No inheritance or estate tax
NZ.description: New Zealand abolished estate duty on 1 January 1993 and gift duty on 1 October 2011. There is no inheritance tax, estate tax, or capital gains tax (with limited exceptions for certain property transactions).
NZ.source: Estate Duty Abolition Act 1993; Taxation (Tax Administration and Remedial Matters) Act 2011
